title: Machine learning predicts C-terminal tails driving calcium-dependent ER protein secretion
summary: Combining computational prediction with machine learning-based models and experimental validation, the authors identified carboxy-terminal sequences of ER resident proteins that diverge from the canonical KDEL retention signal. Molecular modeling and simulations showed that two representative non-canonical retention sequences bind the KDEL receptor stably. The resulting method predicts whether a C-terminal sequence acts as a putative retention signal that is secreted after ER calcium depletion (exodosis). The extent of the experimental validation is not visible in the abstract.
